clue.text: Delightful topping to be used later

indicators.note: topping here means having its top removed, so the opening letter of the phrase goes

parts.note: something kept on ice is saved for later

explanation.surface: A dessert garnish set aside until serving time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' looks like a garnish or British slang for excellent, but here it means cutting the top off ON ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice is a plain synonym for pleasant or lovely, as delightful is.

clue.text: Golf course offering up a couple of slices?

definitions.meaning: Royal St George's, an Open Championship venue, is at a Kent town of this name

definitions.text: offering up a couple of slices?
definitions.meaning: two slices of bread with filling between them

explanation.surface: A golf course with a reputation for players slicing their drives.
explanation.walkthrough: A slice is a golfer's curving miss, which suits the golf surface; the second reading wants slices of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent town hosts a famous links, and the snack made of two bread slices takes its name from an Earl of that title.

clue.text: 1 5 with underwear on, not a sculpture

indicators.note: not tells us the following word a is left out of what has been built

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear
a Nice figure: a number as said in Nice, i.e. French; eleven is onze

explanation.surface: A statue in Nice dressed in underwear, which apparently is no longer art.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 5' reads as NICE FIGURE: a number in the French spoken in Nice. In a down clue 'on' sets the underwear on top; 'not' then drops the A.
explanation.definitionFit: A bronze is a cast metal statue or figure, so the word names a kind of sculpture.

clue.text: 1 5 supporting local officer's first baby

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting puts the French number beneath the other pieces

parts.note: a local is a British pub, an inn

indicators.note: first selects just the opening letter of officer's

parts.note: a Nice figure: a hundred in French is cent

explanation.surface: A French number propping up a village policeman's firstborn child.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is British slang for the neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An innocent is someone without guile or guilt, a sense naturally applied to a newborn child.

clue.text: Price fruit higher than flower

indicators.note: in a down clue, higher than puts the fruit above the river

parts.note: a fig is a fruit
a flower is something that flows, a river: the Ure in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Fruit costs more than flowers at the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the crossword's river, here the Yorkshire Ure, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure is a sum or amount of money, as in naming a price for something.

clue.text: Case one of four

definitions.meaning: hearts, clubs, diamonds or spades in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A single item among four in a set.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawsuit brought in court, and any of the four card groupings, share this one word.

clue.text: Material without intro is for backing singer

indicators.note: for backing means the whole assembled string is read backwards
without intro means the opening letter of the material is dropped

parts.note: tartan is a checked woollen material
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bit of fabric sans introduction suits a backing vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing singer' looks like one phrase, but 'for backing' is the turnaround and 'singer' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank of that surname was the famous American crooner of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Old opponent fairly devoid of it

parts.note: someone anti a thing is opposed to it

indicators.note: devoid of means without, so the letters of it are taken out of the synonym for fairly

parts.note: fairly means quite, rather
taken as written

explanation.surface: An old rival who is rather lacking sex appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devoid of it' removes IT from QUITE, leaving QUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Antique as an adjective means belonging to an earlier era, aged or of long ago.

clue.text: See 17
Pretty good sound toys stuffed, tummies originally getting squeezed

indicators.note: getting squeezed means that first letter is pressed into the middle of the jumble
stuffed suggests toys crammed and jumbled, so the letters of sound toys are rearranged
originally picks out the first letter of tummies

explanation.surface: Stuffed toys that make noises, with their bellies being squeezed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuffed' jumbles the toy letters into NOSODUSTY; the initial of 'tummies' is 'getting squeezed' into that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom of understatement meaning fairly decent, better than expected.

clue.text: Out of tune, this tenor most sharp

indicators.note: out of tune suggests the notes are wrong, so the letters of this tenor are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tenor singing off-key, flat or perhaps sharpest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: Sharp in music means above pitch, but here it means prickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Thorny means prickly, so the superlative means the most spiky or barbed.

clue.text: Predict sea changes in old business

indicators.note: changes says the letters of predict sea are reordered

explanation.surface: A forecaster foretelling shifts in the ocean for an old company.
explanation.definitionFit: The historic commerce in pepper, cinnamon and nutmeg between Asia and Europe was a major early business.

clue.text: 1 5, appropriate

definitions.meaning: a Nice figure: sixteen as said in French
to appropriate is to take possession of, grab

explanation.surface: A fitting French number.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 5' reads as NICE FIGURE, a number in the French spoken in Nice.
explanation.definitionFit: The French for sixteen matches the English verb meaning to grab or commandeer.

clue.text: Not a sausage, fight to eat dry dish

parts.note: British slang for nothing at all, so zero, O

indicators.note: to eat means the fight swallows the abbreviation for dry

parts.note: a melee is a confused brawl
TT, teetotal, means not drinking alcohol

explanation.surface: No sausages, just a scrap over a dry meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a sausage' is British for nothing at all; 'Not' looks like a negative but the phrase gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten eggs cooked in a pan make this classic dish, often folded round a filling.

clue.text: See 12 across
See 16 down
Teaching English, shelter dons

indicators.note: dons means puts on, so the shelter wears the letter for English inside it

parts.note: a tent is a shelter

explanation.surface: University dons running an English course while camping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' looks like a noun for university teachers but is the verb to put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a principle or doctrine taught and held, a point of teaching.

clue.text: 1 5 consuming very good source of veal with hot, wet colourful things?

indicators.note: consuming means the French number swallows the following pieces

parts.note: a Nice figure: three in French
pi, short for pious, is crossword slang for very good
veal comes from a calf
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A French numeral eating veal in a steamy climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of veal' looks like a call for V, but it is the animal that veal comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: Brightly patterned aquarium species from warm seas are living things in water, hence wet.

clue.text: Appear late in day having failed in appeal

indicators.note: in places the jumbled day within the word for appeal

parts.note: to plead is to appeal, beg

indicators.note: having failed suggests the day went wrong, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Turning up at the end of the day after an unsuccessful legal appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'late' means dead, not tardy. 'having failed' rearranges DAY into AYD, placed 'in' PLEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign death is to give the appearance of being deceased, the late in late lamented.

clue.text: Supposed musical sheep flipped

indicators.note: flipped means the combination is turned upside down, read backwards in a down light

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A sheep supposedly turning somersaults in a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: TUP is a British dialect word for a ram. EVITATUP is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Putative means commonly assumed or reputed to be so, without proof.

clue.text: Seem not unsettled by last trace of whopping shiner?

indicators.note: by puts the final letter alongside the jumble
last trace of picks the final letter of whopping
unsettled says the letters of seem not are disturbed and reordered

explanation.surface: Someone seemingly unruffled by a huge black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shiner' suggests a black eye, but here it is anything that sparkles.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewel is something that glitters and shines, so this is a playful description of a precious stone.

clue.text: Measuring unit concerned with setter dividing second 1 5

indicators.note: dividing means splitting the French number in two by going into it

parts.note: a Nice figure: four in French
re means about, concerning
the setter refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: A unit of measure involving the compiler splitting up a second.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 5' is a Nice figure, a number in French; the setter is ME as he refers to himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of area, one metre by one metre, used in measuring floors or land.

clue.text: See 19
Current shade up during day

indicators.note: during puts the reversed colour inside the abbreviated day

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday

indicators.note: up in a down light means reading the colour from bottom to top

parts.note: red is a shade, a colour

explanation.surface: Shade rising through the day, perhaps a fashion trend.
explanation.definitionFit: Modern means present-day, of now, as current does.

clue.text: Familiar odd punches beaten by one shot

indicators.note: punches means the word for odd breaks into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: aced: in tennis, beaten by a single unreturnable serve
quaint means odd, old-fashioned

explanation.surface: Someone peculiar throwing punches, flattened by a single blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punches' looks like blows but signals one piece driving into the other; 'one shot' is a tennis ace.
explanation.definitionFit: To be acquainted with something is to know it, as familiar with it does.

clue.text: Hit when good health reduced by half

indicators.note: reduced by half means only the first half of the toast is kept

parts.note: ...-... is a dated British drinking toast, like cheers

explanation.surface: A boxing knock that halved someone's fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good health' looks like fitness but is the toast.
explanation.definitionFit: To chin someone is British slang for punching them on the jaw.

clue.text: See 26
1 5 in public inquiry reportedly went down

indicators.note: reportedly says the hidden French number is to be spoken, giving an English word of the same sound
in means the French number lies hidden within public inquiry

parts.note: carries cinq, five in French, the Nice figure

explanation.surface: A French number turning up in an official inquiry into a sinking.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 5' is a Nice figure, here five in French, spoken in English.
explanation.definitionFit: Sank is the past tense of sink, meaning dropped or settled beneath the surface.

clue.text: Rip-off in guide, watch my words?

indicators.note: in puts the mixed letters inside the word for guide

parts.note: to lead is to guide

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of rip are mixed

explanation.surface: A tour guide warning against being ripped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch my words' is what a deaf person does by following lip movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who follows speech by observing mouth movements is figuratively watching what is said.

clue.text: 1 5 invested in most uninteresting assessment that's on the way

indicators.note: invested in means the French number is placed inside the next piece

parts.note: driest means most dull, most boring
a Nice figure: twenty in French

explanation.surface: Twenty francs put into the dullest assessment imaginable.
explanation.definitionFit: A test for motorists is literally carried out on the road.
